descriptionChirho: Active destruction by overturning, as in the overthrow of cities (Sodom); Arabic قَلَبَ (qalaba), Korean 뒤집다/엎다, Swahili -pindua/-angusha.
Active causative transformation or conversion of one state to another; Arabic حَوَّلَ (hawwala), Korean 바꾸다/돌이키다, Swahili -geuza/-badilisha.
Intransitive physical turning or turning back in direction; Arabic انصرف/التفت, Korean 돌아서다, Swahili -geuka/-rudi.
Moral or judicial perversion, turning right into wrong; Arabic حَرَّفَ (harrafa), Korean 뒤집다 (moral sense), Swahili -potosha.
Passive or reflexive change of state or condition; Arabic تحوّل/انقلب (tahawwala/inqalaba), Korean 변하다, Swahili -badilika/-geuka.
Passive destruction by overturning, as a city being overthrown; Arabic تُقلَب, Korean 전복되다, Swahili -angushwa.
Reflexive or iterative turning, revolving, or tumbling motion; Arabic يتقلّب/يتدحرج, Korean 굴러가다/돌아가다, Swahili -viringika/-zunguka.
Causative passive of turning, being made to turn by an external agent; a rare stem form of this verb.
